title: 05. Advanced Python: 06 — Context Managers (Deep Dive)
summary: A context manager guarantees setup + teardown around a block. Pattern: acquire resource → use → release, no matter what (success, exception, return, break).

sections.title: 1. What & Why
sections.body:
A context manager guarantees **setup + teardown** around a block. Pattern: acquire resource → use → release, no matter what (success, exception, return, break).

```python
with open("f.txt") as f:
    data = f.read()
# f is closed here, even if read() raised
```

Equivalent without `with`:

```python
f = open("f.txt")
try:
    data = f.read()
finally:
    f.close()
```

sections.title: 2. The protocol
sections.body:
A context manager implements:

- `__enter__(self)` — setup; returns the value bound to `as`.
- `__exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb)` — teardown; returns truthy to **suppress** exception, falsy to **propagate**.

`__exit__`'s 3 args:

- All `None` if block exited normally.
- The exception class, instance, traceback if it raised.

sections.title: 3. Class-based
sections.body:
```python
import time
class Timer:
    def __init__(self, label="block"): self.label = label
    def __enter__(self):
        self.t = time.perf_counter(); return self
    def __exit__(self, et, ev, tb):
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - self.t
        print(f"{self.label}: {elapsed:.3f}s")
        return False                       # don't suppress

with Timer("sort"):
    sorted(range(10**6))
```

If `__exit__` returns `True`, the exception is **silently suppressed**. Use sparingly — usually return `False`/`None`.

sections.title: 4. Generator-based with @contextmanager
sections.body:
```python
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def open_db(url):
    conn = connect(url)
    try:
        yield conn                         # everything before = __enter__
    except Exception:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()                       # everything after = __exit__
```

Rules:

- Exactly **one** `yield`. More than one → `RuntimeError`.
- Wrap user-block code in `try/finally` for cleanup safety.
- Generator-based CMs are **single-use** by default.

sections.title: 5. Multiple context managers
sections.body:
```python
with open("a") as a, open("b") as b:
    ...
```

Equivalent to nested `with`. They're entered left-to-right, exited right-to-left.

### Dynamic stack: `ExitStack`

```python
from contextlib import ExitStack
with ExitStack() as stack:
    files = [stack.enter_context(open(p)) for p in paths]
    ...
# all files closed here, in reverse order
```

Also `stack.callback(fn, *a, **kw)` to register arbitrary cleanup.

sections.title: 6. Built-in context managers (memorize)
sections.body:
| CM                                                                 | Purpose                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `open(...)`                                                        | file                        |
| `threading.Lock/RLock/Semaphore`                                   | acquire/release             |
| `contextlib.suppress(Exc)`                                         | swallow specific exceptions |
| `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io)`                                   | capture print               |
| `contextlib.redirect_stderr(io)`                                   | capture stderr              |
| `contextlib.closing(obj)`                                          | wrap any `.close()` object  |
| `contextlib.nullcontext(obj=None)`                                 | no-op (great as default)    |
| `tempfile.TemporaryFile / NamedTemporaryFile / TemporaryDirectory` | temp files                  |
| `decimal.localcontext()`                                           | local precision             |
| `unittest.mock.patch(...)`                                         | also a decorator            |
| `pytest.raises(Exc)`                                               | assert raises               |
| `warnings.catch_warnings()`                                        | scoped warning filters      |

sections.title: 7. Async context managers (3.5+)
sections.body:
```python
class AsyncDB:
    async def __aenter__(self): ...; return self
    async def __aexit__(self, *exc): ...

async def main():
    async with AsyncDB() as db:
        await db.query(...)
```

Or `@asynccontextmanager`:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
@asynccontextmanager
async def session():
    s = await acquire()
    try: yield s
    finally: await s.close()
```

sections.title: 8. Reentrant / re-usable
sections.body:
- Generator-based CM is **single-use**.
- Class-based CM may be reused if `__enter__` resets state each time.
- `contextlib.ContextDecorator` lets the CM be used as `@decorator` too.

```python
from contextlib import ContextDecorator
class log_call(ContextDecorator):
    def __enter__(self): print("enter"); return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc): print("exit"); return False

@log_call()
def f(): pass

with log_call():
    f()
```

sections.title: 9. nullcontext — the unsung hero
sections.body:
```python
from contextlib import nullcontext
cm = open("f") if filename else nullcontext()
with cm as f:
    ...                                    # works whether f exists or not
```

sections.title: 10. Common pitfalls
sections.body:
- Forgetting `try/finally` inside `@contextmanager` generator → resource leak on exception.
- Returning `True` from `__exit__` accidentally → silent bug.
- Doing heavy work in `__init__` instead of `__enter__` → resource leaks if `with` block never starts.
- Using a generator-based CM twice.
- Missing `await` in async CMs.

sections.title: 11. Patterns
sections.body:
### Transaction

```python
@contextmanager
def transaction(db):
    db.begin()
    try: yield db; db.commit()
    except Exception: db.rollback(); raise
```

### Temporary chdir

```python
import os
@contextmanager
def chdir(path):
    prev = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(path)
    try: yield
    finally: os.chdir(prev)
```

### Capture stdout

```python
import io
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
buf = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(buf):
    print("hi")
captured = buf.getvalue()
```

### Timeit any block

```python
@contextmanager
def timed(label):
    t = time.perf_counter()
    try: yield
    finally: print(label, time.perf_counter() - t)
```

### Lock with timeout

```python
@contextmanager
def acquired(lock, timeout=5):
    if not lock.acquire(timeout=timeout):
        raise TimeoutError
    try: yield
    finally: lock.release()
```
